div.head: Rect 16
div.ab: [16] Be cyswyrhte. Cyswyrhtan gebyreð hundred cyse, ⁊ þæt heo of wringhwæge buteran macige to hlafordes beode; ⁊ hæbbe hire ða syringe ealle butan ðæs hyrdes dæle.
Caseum facienti reddere conuenit centum caseos, et ut butirum faciat ad mensam domini sui de siringie; et habeat sibi totam siringiam preter partem pastoris.
Be cys wyrhte . Cyswyhrtan gebyreð hunded cyse 7 þæt heo of wringhwæge buteran macige to hlafordes beode . 7 hæbbe hire ða syringe ealle butan ðæs hyrdes dæle .
Be cyswyrhte Cyswyrhtan gebyreð hundred cyse, and þæt heo of wringhwæge buteran macige to hlafordes beode; and hæbbe hire ða syringe, ealle butan ðæs hyrdes dæle.

Von der Käsemacherin. Der Käsemacherin gebühren 100 Käse, und dass sie aus Molke, [die enttropft] der Käsepresse, Butter mache für die Herrschaftstafel; und sie erhalte für sich die Buttermilch ganz, ausser jenes Hirten Theil.

Of the cheese-maker. To the cheese-maker are due 100 cheeses, and that she make butter for the lord's table from the whey [that drips] from the cheese-press; and let her have all the buttermilk for herself, except the herdsman's share.

Concerning the cheese-wright To the cheese-wright is due a hundred cheeses and that she make butter from the strained whey for the lord’s table, and she [should] have all the sour milk except the shepherd’s portion.

Regarding the Cheesemaker To the cheesemaker is due one hundred cheeses, and she is to make butter from the strained whey for the lord’s table; and she should keep the buttermilk for herself, all save the shepherd’s share.
div.note: The heading ‘cyswyrhte’ is a Middle English form. The Quadripartitus reads ‘sirin.’ for ‘wring’ (Anglo-Saxon ‘si’ written in ligature resembles ‘ƿ’). K: line breaks removed and a missing full stop after the heading supplied. Liebermann compares Rect 14.

note.seg: sirin. Quadr. [Angelsächsisch si, ligirt geschrieben, ähnelt ƿ]
sirin. Quadr. [Anglo-Saxon si, written as a ligature, resembles ƿ]
Q missversteht, die Käsemacherin habe 100 Käse zu liefern (wie 5. 5, 1), so Andrews.—Ein cheeseland unter St. Augustins zu Canterbury bei Vinogradoff Vill. 257.—Vgl. Gl Käse 6

Q misunderstands this as meaning that the cheese-maker had to deliver 100 cheeses (as in 5. 5, 1); so Andrews.—A cheeseland belonging to St Augustine's, Canterbury, in Vinogradoff Vill. 257.—Cf. Gl Käse 6

Nicht ‘Rahm, saure Sahne’ (Leo) oder ‘dicke Milch’ (Schmid), sondern ‘whey pressed out of cheese’ (Toller; Andrews 233) oder vielmehr ‘dropping out of the cheesewrings’; Tho. Hardy (Tess of the d’Urb. 164. 210) aus heutigem Wessex. Vgl. bei Toller winwringe: ‘torcular prælum [noch dialektisch s. Wright s. v. wring]’, wringan ‘Feuchtigkeit auspressen’ (nicht ‘buttern’), mnddt. wringen ‘(geronnene Milch zu Käse) pressen’; Lübben; Schade

Not ‘cream, sour cream’ (Leo) or ‘thick milk’ (Schmid), but ‘whey pressed out of cheese’ (Toller; Andrews 233), or rather ‘dropping out of the cheesewrings’; Tho. Hardy (Tess of the d’Urb. 164. 210), from present-day Wessex. Cf. in Toller winwringe: ‘torcular prælum [still in dialect, see Wright s. v. wring]’, wringan ‘to press out moisture’ (not ‘to churn’), MLG wringen ‘to press (curdled milk into cheese)’; Lübben; Schade

Nicht ‘auf des Herrn Gebot’ (Schmid). Vgl. mensa dominorum (Mat. 15, 27): hlaforda beodum. Die Domäne heisst (wie dt. Tafelgut) bordland bei Bracton f. 263 und in Schottland; G. Neilson Scot. rev. 1898 p. 236

Not ‘at the lord's command’ (Schmid). Cf. mensa dominorum (Mat. 15, 27): hlaforda beodum. The demesne is called bordland (like German Tafelgut) in Bracton f. 263 and in Scotland; G. Neilson Scot. rev. 1898 p. 236
